lines.text: The next evening. Fog rolls in off the harbor, and Pip walks the quay holding the trumpet case very casually, like a normal bag for normal things.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: [Old fish auction. Door with no handle. Knock twice, hum a B-flat. Unless it's a trap. Or a prank. Or just a door.]

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: Pip! There you are. Half the harbor's been talking about your getaway.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Oh. Um. Hi, Gus. Did they fine you?

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: Forty coins and a leaflet about inner peace. Worth it. My haddock haven't been this happy in years.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: [Forty coins. Because of me. Very peaceful.]

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: Listen. The auction square is crawling with the Squad tonight. You won't walk past them on your own.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: Same way you stopped the whole market yesterday. Play. Folk round here can't help themselves. They'll come and stand round you, thick as a sea wall.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: Mind the needle, though. Every note shows up on their meters. Play too long and they'll come looking right where they heard it.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: [Play a little. Walk while they're still humming along. Stop before the meters twitch. Simple. Terrifying, but simple.]
Down the quay, a grey uniform turns slowly, sweeping a decibel meter through the fog like a lighthouse.

lines.speaker: mute
lines.text: Sergeant, I'm reading a faint thirty decibels near the bollards. Possibly a gull. Possibly a suspect gull.

lines.speaker: mute
lines.text: Sorry, Sergeant. Drone and Partners called again, asking for hourly readings. I wasn't aware they were our superiors.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: That's my cue to be a very boring fishmonger. Go on, Pip. Make some friends.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: [Make friends. In public. With a trumpet. Okay, feet. You did it once.]
